tagline.text: The Philippines' only underground cemetery, where revolutionaries once met in secret

location.label: Location
location.text: Bambang, Nagcarlan, Laguna (at the foot of Mount Banahaw)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (dry season, November–May, is easiest for travel)

children.text: A baroque-style cemetery built in

by a Franciscan friar, with an underground crypt beneath its chapel — the only underground cemetery in the Philippines. With its red brick walls, arched gate, and the underground chamber once used as a secret meeting place for revolutionaries, all free to explore, it's often ranked as the highlight of a trip through Laguna's mountain towns.

Nagcarlan Underground Cemetery is a Spanish colonial-era burial ground in the small town of Nagcarlan, at the foot of Mount Banahaw in eastern Laguna province. It sits in the village of Bambang, about
2km
south of the town center, and was built in

under the supervision of Franciscan missionary Father Vicente Velloc. It was part of the same building campaign that extensively rebuilt the town's San Bartolome Church and raised a convent around the same time.

Red brick and plastered walls enclose the roughly one-hectare circular cemetery, lined on the inside with niche tombs stacked like drawers. At the end of the brick path stands a baroque chapel; a staircase inside leads down to a crypt about
underground. This is where Spanish priests and prominent local families were once laid to rest, with about 240 above-ground niches and 36 underground tombs, for roughly 270 graves in total.
This cemetery also holds an important place in Philippine revolutionary history. In

, leaders of the Katipunan, Laguna's secret revolutionary society, held clandestine meetings in this underground chamber, out of sight of the Spanish authorities, and it later served as a hideout for guerrillas and residents during the Philippine-American War and World War II. The Philippine government declared it a National Historical Landmark by presidential decree in
, and it's now run as a museum by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP), owned by the Diocese of San Pablo. No new burials take place here.
Touring the cemetery itself takes only
30 minutes–1 hour

, but combining it with the cool mountain town of Nagcarlan and the old churches and waterfalls of neighboring Liliw and Majayjay makes for a full and rewarding day trip. It's especially recommended for travelers interested in Spanish-era architecture and Philippine history, those looking for a quiet, unusual spot off the beaten path, and photography lovers.

blocks.title: The arched gate and brick wall

children.text: The baroque arched gate on the roadside is the cemetery's face. Through the arch, the brick path and chapel line up straight ahead, making this the best spot for the classic photo.
Following the stairs inside the chapel down, old tombs and a small altar appear in the cool air. Picture the revolutionaries gathering here by lamplight.

blocks.title: The chapel's altar and sacred images

children.text: Inside the chapel stands a neoclassical altar and an image of Christ lying in the tomb. Liturgies are still held here on special occasions such as Holy Week and the Feast of Christ the King.

blocks.title: The niche tombs and old inscriptions

children.text: The niches lining the wall bear Spanish and Tagalog inscriptions dating back to the late 19th century. It's rewarding to stroll slowly and read the names of old families.

The old church in Nagcarlan town proper stands out for its red brick facade and Moorish-style crenellations. Rebuilt around the same time as the cemetery, it continues the same story when seen together.
In the woods on the outskirts of Nagcarlan, a modest waterfall drops in two streams. It's a good spot to rest and dip your feet in the cold mountain water.
The neighboring town of Liliw is known for handmade sandals and slippers. Shops line the main street, making it easy to pick up cheap, sturdy footwear as a souvenir.

blocks.title: The newly refurbished museum exhibition hall

children.text: The National Historical Commission of the Philippines renovated the cemetery and museum and reopened them in
December 2025

. The new exhibition hall covers the cemetery's history, excavated artifacts, the restoration process, and Philippine funeral culture, so stopping there before touring the grounds deepens your understanding.

items.title: A full day
items.subtitle: A trip through the mountain towns of Nagcarlan and Liliw

children.text: Depart Manila (by car, or bus bound for San Pablo)
Arrive in Nagcarlan, tour the underground cemetery (gate, chapel, underground crypt)
Explore San Bartolome Church in town
Lunch in Nagcarlan or Liliw
Browse and shop on Liliw's sandal street, visit Liliw Church
Rest at Bunga Falls, or stop by the old church in Majayjay
Depart for Manila via San Pablo
The cemetery closes around
4 PM

and is closed on Mondays, so it's best to visit in the morning. If traveling by public transport, sticking to the cemetery, the church, and Liliw and skipping the waterfall still makes for a full day.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Cemetery and church only, by private car

children.text: Leave Manila and take the SLEX toward San Pablo
Arrive at Nagcarlan and see the museum exhibition hall first
Photograph the front gate arch, then look around the chapel, the underground ossuary, and the niche tombs
Explore San Bartolome Church in town
Lunch in San Pablo and buy buko pie
Head back to Manila, arriving in the late afternoon
Take a bus bound for San Pablo or Lucena from Pasay Buendia or Cubao and get off in San Pablo. It takes about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
, for around
one way.

Buses to Lucena by DLTB, JAC Liner, and JAM Liner leave frequently from Cubao, Buendia, and PITX. Just tell the conductor you're getting off at "SM San Pablo," and since provincial bus fares rose per km from
September 28, 2026
, the fare may be slightly higher.
In San Pablo town, transfer to a jeepney bound for Nagcarlan, about
30–45 minutes
, for around
. If you took a bus to Santa Cruz, Laguna instead, you can also catch a jeepney to Nagcarlan from there.
Jeepney service drops off sharply in the evening. Line up your return transport no later than
5 PM
From Nagcarlan town proper to the cemetery is about
5–10 minutes
by tricycle, for about
. To cover the cemetery, the church, Bunga Falls, and Liliw all in one trip, it's more convenient to charter a tricycle for half a day, negotiated at around
The easiest route is to take SLEX toward San Pablo, then head up from San Pablo town to Nagcarlan. It's about
from Manila, taking about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
. You can also go via Calamba and Los Baños along the lakeshore road, but city traffic there is frequent. There's a small parking area in front of the cemetery.
The cemetery is open for visits year-round. Nagcarlan sits high at the foot of Mount Banahaw, so it's a bit cooler than Manila, and the dry season,
November–May
, with less rain, is best if you also want to enjoy the waterfall and a walk around town. During
December–February
, morning and evening temperatures drop to around
, pleasant for a drive.
During the
June–October

rainy season, afternoon rain is frequent in this mountainous area, and the crypt's stairs and the brick path become slippery. After heavy rain, the path to Bunga Falls turns muddy and the current gets rough, so it's best to skip the waterfall then.
Around Holy Week (
late March–April
) and All Saints'/All Souls' Day (
November 1–2

), liturgies and visitors create a special atmosphere, but the visiting route may be restricted or hours may change. For a quiet visit, weekday mornings are best; check the NHCP museum's official page for the latest notices before you go.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
There aren't many places to stay in Nagcarlan town proper; small resorts with pools are scattered around the outskirts and toward neighboring Rizal and Liliw, at about
per night. For more options, staying at a hotel in San Pablo town, about
30–45 minutes
away by car, and enjoying a lakeside walk in San Pablo, the "City of Seven Lakes," is also a good choice. Most travelers visit from Manila as a day trip.

Nagcarlan and Liliw town proper have Filipino home-style restaurants and snack shops. In Laguna's mountain towns, popular souvenirs include sweet coconut candies, espasol (a cylindrical rice cake), and uraro, a crisp cookie made from arrowroot flour. San Pablo, a coconut-growing area, is known for buko pie and coconut desserts, and lakeside restaurants serve tilapia, a freshwater fish. Along Liliw's main street, small cafes selling cold drinks and snacks sit between the sandal shops.
Operating hours run roughly Tuesday to Sunday,
9 AM–4 PM
, closed on Mondays and some holidays. Check the NHCP museum's official page before you go.
Admission is free, and you'll sign a guestbook at the entrance. Ask a staff member on duty for a brief explanation.
The underground crypt is dimly lit with narrow stairs. Wear non-slip shoes, and a phone flashlight comes in handy.
The chapel and the underground space are still considered sacred. Don't talk loudly or climb onto the tombs for photos.
The most popular shot frames the chapel through the front arch. Soft morning light brings out the color of the brick best.
Public transport involves long transfer times. If you're in a group, chartering a tricycle or van in San Pablo saves time and energy.
Many shops and tricycles in town take cash only. Bring plenty of small bills.
Opening hours, temporary closures, and Holy Week liturgy schedules are posted first on the museum's
official Facebook page
. Check it once the day before your visit.
The cemetery is often closed on Mondays and holidays, and may also close temporarily for repairs or events. Check the latest notices so you don't make the trip for nothing.
The underground crypt has a low ceiling and narrow passages, which can be uncomfortable for those with claustrophobia or limited mobility.
The inscriptions and walls are fragile heritage. Don't touch or lean on them, and never write graffiti or light candles.
The mountain road between Nagcarlan and Liliw has many sharp curves. Slow down while driving, and avoid driving at night.
During the rainy season, the rocks around Bunga Falls get very slippery and the water can rise suddenly. Avoid swimming at the falls after rain.
